story.title: From Tuna Canneries to Recycled Nets: Oman Commits OMR 13.39 Million to Coastal Fisheries
story.seo_title: Oman Signs OMR 13.39M Deals for Fish Canning & Net Recycling
story.meta_description: Oman invests OMR 13.39 million in four fisheries projects across Duqm and Al-Musannah, including tuna and sardine canneries and fishing net recycling.

detail.extracted_title: From Tuna Canneries to Recycled Nets: Oman Commits OMR 13.39 Million to Coastal Fisheries
detail.excerpt: Four new investment agreements across Al-Wusta and South Al-Batinah pair industrial tuna, sardine, and demersal fish canning plants with a circular-economy facility to recycle discarded fishing nets.
detail.article_html:
Along the 3,165-kilometer coastline of the Sultanate of Oman, fishing has sustained coastal communities for millennia. For much of the modern era, however, a substantial share of Oman's daily catch left local ports as unprocessed raw fish, leaving the higher economic returns of canning, packaging, and industrial processing to overseas markets. At the same time, worn nylon and polyethylene fishing nets accumulated in harbor yards and coastal waters, posing a persistent environmental challenge for artisanal and commercial fleets alike.

On Wednesday, the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources took a decisive step to address both challenges simultaneously, signing four investment agreements totaling OMR 13.39 million across the governorates of Al-Wusta and South Al-Batinah. Signed on behalf of the Ministry by Eng. Yaqoub bin Khalfan Al-Busaidi, Undersecretary for Fisheries, the agreements link commercial harvesting directly to onshore canning plants and introduce a dedicated industrial facility for recycling spent fishing nets.

Two Major Canning Plants Anchor the Duqm Fisheries Zone

More than OMR 11 million of the new capital is concentrated in the Fisheries Industries Zone in Wilayat Duqm, Al-Wusta Governorate, positioning the Arabian Sea port as a primary processing hub for Indian Ocean catches.

The first agreement, valued at OMR 5.36 million, establishes an integrated project for commercial fishing and onshore canning of demersal (bottom-dwelling) fish in the Duqm Fisheries Zone. By uniting offshore harvesting vessels with a dedicated processing and canning plant under one operational roof, the project stabilizes raw-material supply chains and raises the export value of Omani demersal stocks.

The second agreement commits OMR 5.73 million—the largest single investment in the package—to build a specialized tuna and sardine canning factory in the Duqm Fisheries Zone. Designed as an integrated coastal fishing and manufacturing operation, the plant will process high-demand pelagic species caught off Al-Wusta's coast into shelf-stable canned products for domestic food security and international export.

Expanding Value-Added Processing in Al-Musannah

Further north on the Sea of Oman coast, the third agreement directs OMR 2 million toward constructing a fish processing and canning plant in Wilayat Al-Musannah in South Al-Batinah Governorate. Situated near established Batinah landing sites and major domestic transport corridors, the Al-Musannah facility will process catches from local coastal fishermen, expanding downstream manufacturing jobs and strengthening supply links between traditional fishing boats and regional retail markets.

Turning Spent Fishing Nets into Circular Industrial Value

While the first three agreements focus on food production, the fourth agreement introduces an important circular-economy model to Oman's marine sector. With an investment of OMR 300,000 in Al-Wusta Governorate, the project will establish a specialized facility to collect and recycle consumed and damaged fishing nets.

Instead of allowing discarded nets to burden municipal landfills or threaten marine habitats through ghost fishing, the facility will convert worn synthetic nets into secondary raw materials for manufacturing. Together, the four projects illustrate how Oman's fisheries strategy is evolving: capturing greater industrial value from every ton of tuna, sardines, and demersal fish landed in Duqm and Al-Musannah, while keeping the waters that sustain those fisheries clean for future generations.

detail.instagram_caption:
The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has signed four new investment agreements worth OMR 13.39 million across the governorates of Al-Wusta and South Al-Batinah, linking commercial fishing directly with domestic canning factories and circular-economy marine recycling.

In the Duqm Fisheries Industries Zone, two major projects—an OMR 5.73 million tuna and sardine cannery and an OMR 5.36 million demersal fish harvesting and canning facility—will process Arabian Sea catches onshore rather than exporting them raw. A third OMR 2 million processing and canning plant will serve coastal landings in Wilayat Al-Musannah, while a fourth OMR 300,000 facility in Al-Wusta will recycle worn and discarded fishing nets into industrial raw materials.

How can circular-economy initiatives like fishing net recycling transform coastal industries across Oman?

Read the full analysis at omanspire.om (link in bio).

slides.h: Four coastal agreements linking fishing fleets to onshore factories
p: Signed by {{Eng. Yaqoub bin Khalfan Al-Busaidi}}, Undersecretary for Fisheries, the [[OMR 13.39 million package]] establishes three fish processing and canning plants alongside a [[marine net recycling facility]] across {{Al-Wusta and South Al-Batinah}}.

slides.h: Over OMR 11 million for tuna, sardine, and demersal canning in Duqm
p: The {{Duqm Fisheries Industries Zone}} anchors two flagship factories: an [[OMR 5.73 million tuna and sardine cannery]] and an [[OMR 5.36 million demersal fishing and canning plant]] to maximize domestic value.

slides.h: OMR 2 million fish processing and canning plant in Al-Musannah
p: On the Sea of Oman coast, a third agreement commits [[OMR 2 million]] to build a fish processing and canning factory in {{Wilayat Al-Musannah}}, connecting South Al-Batinah fishermen directly to value-added food production.

slides.h: Circular economy at sea: recycling spent fishing nets in Al-Wusta
p: An [[OMR 300,000 circular-economy project]] in {{Al-Wusta Governorate}} will collect and recycle [[discarded fishing nets]], converting worn marine gear into secondary industrial materials and protecting coastal ecosystems.
